Systeme | Nexla Docs
highlights:
## Prerequisites ​

Nexla connects to the Systeme.io Public API with a public API key from your Systeme.io account. Systeme authenticates every request with this key, sent in the `X-API-Key` request header. To create a key:

1. Sign in to your Systeme.io account.
2. Click your profile picture, and select Settings.
3. In the left menu, select MCP & API keys.
4. In the Public API keys section, click Create.
5. Enter a unique name for the key and, optionally, an expiration date and time. Leave the Expiration field empty to keep the key active indefinitely, and click Save.
6. Copy the key immediately. Systeme shows the key only once, right after you create it; if you did not copy it, delete the key and create a new one.

An account can hold up to three public API keys, and Systeme sends an email notification each time a key is created. The key gives access to all of your account's data, so keep it confidential. For details, see Systeme's How to use the systeme.io public API help article.

Systeme API rate limits

Systeme applies a rate limit that is shared by all of the API keys on your account. Requests over the limit receive an HTTP `429 Too Many Requests` response with a `Retry-After` header. Templates that page through large collections, such as contacts, make one request per page of 100 records. See the rate-limiting section of the Systeme Public API documentation for details.

## Authenticate ​

### Credentials required ​

An authentication method that requires sending a unique secret token with each API request

| Field | Required | Secret | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API Key Value | Yes | Yes | An encoded string value used as a secret token to authenticate API requests |

### Create a credential in Nexla ​

1. After selecting the data source/destination type, click the Add Credential tile to open the Add New Credential overlay.
2. Enter a name for the credential in the Credential Name field and a short, meaningful description in the Credential Description field.
3. Enter your Systeme public API key in the API Key Value field. This is the key you created in Prerequisites. Nexla sends it in the `X-API-Key` header of every request to the Systeme API.

If your API key is compromised, delete it in Systeme under Settings > MCP & API keys, create a new one, and update the API Key Value on this credential.
4. Click the Save button at the bottom of the overlay. The newly added credential will now appear in a tile on the Authenticate screen during data source/destination creation.

Nexla tests the credential by reading the contact list from your Systeme account.

highlights:
# How to use the systeme.io public API (Application Programming Interface)

Play: YouTube video

In this article, you will learn how to configure and use the systeme.io public API, including how to generate API keys and what actions you can perform.

## 1. What is an API?

The acronym API stands for "Application Programming Interface", a series of instructions by which a platform offers services to other platforms. It's a strategic gateway for external developers, enabling them to access specific functionality or data from a platform in a structured, secure way. It's like a set of ready-to-use tools that make it easy to build new applications, services, or combinations.

In short, systeme.io opens up to other platforms to offer its services where it has added value.

## 2. How does our public API work?

Our API exposes a carefully selected set of features, enabling developers to interact with our platform transparently and efficiently. If you'd like to know more about how it works, you can read our official API documentation.

## 3. How to generate your API keys

API keys are unique identifiers that authenticate requests to our public API. They enable you to programmatically access and manage various resources on our platform.

To connect an external integration, you first need to generate a secure API key. Click on your profile picture and select Settings (1). In the left menu, click MCP & API keys (2).

Scroll down to the Public API keys section and click Create (3).

Give your key a name, set an expiration date, and click Save (4).

> Note: To keep your API key active indefinitely, leave the 'Expiration' field empty.

Your key is now ready.

## 4. What can you do with our API?

Our API opens up some interesting possibilities. Below you will find the main actions you can perform using our public API:

a. Contacts, tags, and custom field management:

- Contacts: Create new contacts, update existing ones, list your audience with advanced filters, or delete contacts.
- Tags: Create, assign, list, and remove tags from contacts.
- Custom fields: Retrieve available contact custom fields and their identifiers (slugs) to correctly fill in contact information.

b. Newsletters and campaigns management:

- Newsletters: Create new drafts, update existing ones, target audiences (using include/exclude tags), configure sender details, schedule or remove scheduling, send test emails, send newsletters directly, delete drafts, and fetch specific newsletters.
- Campaigns: Create, retrieve, update, and delete entire email campaigns, as well as individual campaign steps.
- Email statistics: Retrieve performance statistics for your newsletters, campaign emails, and automation emails. You can fetch totals for a specific period (up to 31 days) with a daily breakdown, results for each email sent during that period, or all-time results for a specific email. Statistics include sends, opens, clicks, bounces, and spam reports.

c. Funnels and Page editor management:

- Create funnels, opt-in steps, and webinar funnels: Easily create new funnels, add opt-in steps to your funnels, and create webinar funnels with all the necessary webinar steps, including registration, thank you, and webinar broadcast pages.
- List and retrieve funnels: Browse through your existing funnels, opt-in steps, and webinar pages, or search for specific ones.
- Regenerate page content (webinar pages): Regenerate the full content of a webinar page.
- Page editor: Save generated page content directly to your funnel steps or website pages (full replace), retrieve JSON schemas for specific page types, and regenerate webinar page content.

> Notes:
> 
> - Currently, modifying (editing) funnels and funnel steps via MCP is not supported.
> - Deleting funnels, funnel steps, and webinar pages through MCP is also not supported at this time
> - AI can regenerate the content of a webinar page by replacing the full content, but small targeted edits are not currently supported.

d. Price plans and coupon management:

- Create, edit, and delete: Generate new price plans and coupons, or partially update and delete existing ones.
- List and search: Browse through all your existing price plans and coupons, or fetch specific items by their ID.

j. Course management:

- Courses: Create, edit settings, delete, list, retrieve, activate, and deactivate courses. List course page templates and choose a theme for your course.
- Modules: Create, edit, delete, list, and retrieve modules to structure your courses.
- Lectures: Create, edit, delete, add delays, enable comments, list, retrieve, activate, and deactivate lectures.

> Note on courses: Support for course bundles will be added in future updates.

f. Community management:

- Communities: Retrieve a list of your existing communities and access a list of the current members within a specific community.
- Invite members: Programmatically invite new users to join your communities by providing their contact ID.

g. Automation rules management:

- Create automation rules: Easily connect common events and actions without configuring them manually in your dashboard. Currently, you can create rules using the following triggers: Tags (Tag added, Tag removed), Courses (Enrolled in course, Course completed, Lecture completed, Module completed), Sales (Subscription payment failed, New sale, Sale canceled), Funnel form subscribed, Campaign completed, Booking created, and Page visited. And the following actions: Tags (Add a tag, Remove a tag), Courses (Enroll in course, Revoke access to course), Unsubscribe from campaign, Send webhook, and Send SMS.
- List and retrieve automation rules: Browse your automation rules or fetch a specific rule by its ID.

h. Subscriptions management:

- Subscriptions: Retrieve a list of all resources in a subscription from third-party platforms, and cancel a subscription either immediately or at the end of the billing cycle.

i. Webhook management:

- Programmatically create new webhooks to receive real-time notifications, retrieve lists of your existing webhooks, and remove webhooks that are no longer needed.

j. Digital product management:

- Create, view, update, and delete: Fully manage your digital products.
- List and search: Browse your existing digital products or search for specific ones.
- Link price plans: Programmatically create or link price plans directly to your digital products.
- Connect to selling flows: Programmatically connect digital products to your selling flows (order forms, upsells, downsells).

k. Physical product management:

- Create, view, update, retrieve, and delete: Fully manage your physical products.
- Connect to selling flows: Programmatically connect physical products to your selling flows (order forms, upsells, downsells).

l. Offers and sales settings management:

- Create and configure offers: Set up offers for your selling flows, such as order forms, upsells, and downsells.
- Manage sales settings: Configure detailed settings for your offers, including coupons, order bumps, currency, payment methods, tax settings, affiliate commissions, payout delays, and sales limits. You can also easily attach your digital and physical products directly to these offers.

m. Calendar bookings management:

- Create, update, and delete events: Generate new booking calendar events, or easily modify and delete existing ones.
- List and search events: Retrieve a list of your booking calendar events or search for specific ones by name.
- Retrieve event details: Fetch full details for a specific event, including its locations, availability, time zone, date range, and reminders.
- List and filter bookings: Retrieve a list of your calendar bookings and filter them by event, status, and date range.

> Note on calendar events: Updating an existing calendar event's type is not currently supported through MCP.

n. SMS template management:

- Create, edit, and delete: Generate new SMS templates, or modify and remove existing ones you no longer need.
- List and search: Retrieve a list of your existing SMS templates or search for specific ones.

> Notes:
> 
> - To easily identify and manage your tokens, each must have a unique name.
> - A token can only be copied immediately after creating it. If you forgot to copy your token, delete it and create a new one.
> - As a security measure, we will send you an email notification whenever a new public API key is created in your systeme.io account.
> - You can create up to 3 API keys per account.

Last updated on October 12, 2026

## Frequently asked questions about systeme.io pricing

How does systeme.io pricing work and what do I get on each plan?

Systeme.io has four plans based primarily on contact limits. Free: 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, 1 course. Startup ($17/month): 5,000 contacts, 10 sales funnels, 5 courses. Webinar ($47/month): 10,000 contacts, 50 sales funnels, 20 courses, plus evergreen webinars. Unlimited ($97/month): unlimited contacts, funnels, courses and automation rules. All plans include unlimited email sends, unlimited sub-accounts, 0% transaction fees, and the same set of core tools.

Does systeme.io have a free plan and what are its limits?

Yes, the free plan supports up to 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, 1 blog, 1 course, 1 affiliate program, and 1 custom domain. Emails sent are unlimited. The free plan never expires and does not require a credit card. Other features have lower limits on the free plan, like 1 automation rule, 1 email campaign and 500 students. If you need more, the Startup plan at $17/month is the next step.

Which systeme.io pricing plan should I choose for my business size?

Under 2,000 contacts: use the free plan. It costs nothing and covers most needs. 2,000 to 5,000 contacts: Startup at $17/month. 5,000 to 10,000 contacts: Webinar at $47/month (also adds evergreen webinars). Over 10,000 contacts: Unlimited at $97/month.

...

Can I change or cancel my systeme.io plan at any time and what happens to my data?

Yes. You can upgrade your plan or cancel your subscription at any time from your account settings. If you cancel, you keep your current plan until your next billing date, then your account reverts to the free plan. To downgrade, you have two options: contact our support team to convert the remaining days of your current plan into the lower plan, or cancel your current plan, wait until your account reverts to the free plan on your next billing date, then upgrade to the plan you want

## Frequently asked questions about the systeme.io MCP server

What is the systeme.io MCP server and how does it help me?

The systeme.io MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a standard that securely connects your systeme.io account to AI assistants like ChatGPT or Claude. It allows you to interact with your business data using natural language, enabling you to build funnels, manage contacts, and create email campaigns just by typing simple commands in your chat window.

Is it safe to connect my systeme.io account to AI tools?

Yes. We prioritize your security by using a secure authentication process. When you connect via MCP, you are in control of the permissions granted to the AI. You can choose which tools the AI can access (read-only vs. write/delete) and revoke that access at any time directly from your AI provider’s settings.

Do I need to be a developer to use the MCP server?

Not at all. While the MCP standard is built for developers, our direct integration allows you to connect your account to ChatGPT or Claude in just a few clicks. No coding is required; you simply authorize the connection, and you’re ready to start using AI to manage your systeme.io workspace.

Can the AI perform any action on my account?

You are in control. You can configure permission levels for each tool the AI uses: Always allow, Needs approval, or Blocked. For sensitive operations (like creating or deleting contacts, price plans, or coupons), the AI will require your confirmation within the chat before executing any command.

Which systeme.io plans include access to the MCP server?

The MCP server is a powerful feature included in all systeme.io plans. Whether you are on our Free, Startup, Webinar, or Unlimited plan, you can connect your account to AI tools and start leveraging the power of natural language to streamline your marketing and business management.

# How to connect your systeme.io account to ChatGPT using MCP keys

In this article, you will learn how to integrate the systeme.io MCP server with ChatGPT so you can interact with your account data using AI.

What you will need:

- A systeme.io account
- An MCP key generated from your systeme.io account (How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protoco l)
- A ChatGPT account

To connect systeme.io to ChatGPT using an MCP key, log in to your ChatGPT account, open the left side menu, and click Plugins (1).

Click Add (2), and select Add custom MCP server (3).

In the setup popup, enter the following details:

- Name (4): Systeme.io MCP
- Description (optional) (5): Systeme.io official MCP server
- Connection (6): Server URL
- Server URL (7): https://mcp.systeme.io/mcp?mcpKey=YOUR_KEY

> Note: Replace YOUR_KEY with the MCP key you created on your systeme.io account.

- Authentication (8): No Authentication

Tick the I understand and want to continue box (9), then click Create as a plugin (10).

In the "Add Systeme.io MCP server to ChatGPT" window, click Connect systeme.io (11).

Once connected and set up, start a new chat in ChatGPT and start using commands to interact with your systeme.io account.

> Notes:
> 
> - some actions (like create/update/delete) may be restricted or require additional confirmation. See ChatGPT permissions and action restrictions.
> 
> - If the server fails to connect, ensure that:
> 
> - Your MCP key is valid and not expired, and you correctly provided it to the server.
> - Developer Mode is active in your ChatGPT settings.

You can also connect your systeme.io account to ChatGPT using the direct app connection. If you prefer this option over a manual setup with MCP keys, follow this guide: How to connect your systeme.io account to ChatGPT.

Last updated on November 9, 2026

mcp.title: What is the systeme.io MCP server? · Plain Funnels
highlights:
By Philip Borrowman · Published 4 September 2026· Updated 11 September 2026

MCP is an open standard for connecting an AI assistant to an outside platform. systeme.io runs an MCP server, so a chat window can read and change your account when you type a sentence at it.

## What the letters mean

MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. systeme.io describes it as an open standard designed to connect AI models with outside data and tools.

It is not a systeme.io invention and not a systeme.io feature you use inside the dashboard. It is a shared format, and systeme.io has built a server that speaks it.

## The two ends of it

systeme.io describes the server as a bridge between two things.

- The host: your AI tool, for example ChatGPT or Claude.
- The server: your systeme.io account.

Without that bridge, an instruction typed at an AI tool stops in the chat window. It can write you an email, but it cannot put that email into systeme.io.

## What connecting it actually gets you

Typing instead of clicking. Once connected, an instruction in ordinary English runs against your real account.

systeme.io's own documented examples read like this.

- List the last 20 contacts.
- Create a new tag named 'New Leads'.
- Create a new funnel named 'Summer campaign'.
- Update the subject line of the summer sale newsletter.

The work happens in the chat window. The result appears in the systeme.io dashboard.

...

One MCP key, generated inside systeme.io.

Click your profile picture, choose

...

The connection address is https://mcp.systeme.io/mcp?mcpKey=YOURMCPKEY, with your own key in place of the last part.

...

ChatGPT is rougher. systeme.io states it has no official ChatGPT application and that access to the MCP server is in beta, so the server can only be added through ChatGPT's Developer mode, as a custom app using the same URL with authentication set to No Auth.

## What state the feature is in

systeme.io calls it an initial release. Its developer documentation carries a status notice saying the same thing and that capabilities and stability are still being worked on.

Two consequences are documented. OAuth, which systeme.io names as the recommended authentication method, is not supported yet and is planned. And systeme.io says you may run into minor stability issues in the meantime.

mcp.title: Systeme.io MCP: We Gave an AI Agent the Keys (Free Plan) | Hayka Pacha
highlights:
November 13, 2026  · 7 min read 

We gave an AI agent a systeme.io MCP key on a free account. It built an email-capture funnel in about 100 seconds, then an automation rule in 82 seconds on the second round. The free plan refused the next rule, and our first test sign-up got no welcome email, while the second one did. We ran the test on November 13, 2026 with Claude Code on a free systeme.io account, no credit card.

This is a test of what an agent actually gets for free, not a tutorial on MCP. Every number below comes from our own run. How we test explains why our agents, not a person, do the testing.

## What is the systeme.io MCP server?

It’s a server that lets an AI agent drive your systeme.io account through a set of tools. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the open standard for plugging tools into an agent, described on modelcontextprotocol.io. Systeme.io runs its own server, and it’s in the free plan.

The key is created in Settings > Connections > MCP & API keys. You name it, set an expiry date, and you can hold two. The key goes into the server address (`https://mcp.systeme.io/mcp?mcpKey=YOUR_KEY`), which you add to your agent. Ours was Claude Code.

We asked the server what it offers: `initialize` answered “Systeme.io MCP server” version 0.1.0, and `tools/list` returned 171 tools. Contacts, tags, funnels and their pages, automation rules, emails, newsletters, campaigns, courses, products, coupons, calendar, communities, SMS. Treat the key like a password: whoever holds it controls the account.

...

The server refused: “This email address must be verified and eligible for use as a marketing sender”. Our address showed as Verified in Settings > Emails, with a warning: to send from it, you must authenticate its domain.

...

## Round two: an email and an automation rule in 82 seconds

Same account, a new prompt: 18 calls, 82 seconds. We asked for the welcome email from our own address, then a rule sending it when someone subscribes through the funnel’s form, then a second rule. This time the server accepted our sender address.

The first rule went live: trigger “form subscribed”, action “send email”. The second was refused with the exact message “Automation rules limit reached”.

mcp.title: How to manage your contacts with the systeme.io MCP server | systeme.io Help Center
highlights:
In this article, you will learn how to manage your systeme.io contacts using natural language through our native MCP server. By connecting an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude, you can add, update, and organize your contacts seamlessly without leaving your chat window.

What you will need:

- A systeme.io account
- An MCP key generated from your systeme.io account (How to use the systeme.io MCP server (Model Context Protocol))
- An AI tool connected to your systeme.io account using MCP keys:

- How to connect your systeme.io account with Claude using MCP keys
- How to connect your systeme.io account with ChatGPT using MCP keys

Once your AI tool is connected to the systeme.io MCP server, you can manage your contacts using simple, natural language prompts.

## 1. Managing contacts

The MCP server allows you to perform basic actions on your contacts directly from the chat. Provide the required details (such as an email address) and specify the action you want to perform.

a. Create a contact: You can ask the AI to add a new contact to your list.

Example: Create the following contact: John Doe, systemeio.help.demo@gmail.com, (202) 555-0123.

b. Update a contact: If you need to change a contact's information, simply provide the contact's email and the new details to the AI.

Example: Update contact for systemeio.help.demo@gmail.com, change their name to "Sami" and the phone number to "+12345678."

c. List and retrieve contacts: You can use the AI to filter your lists or fetch specific contact details without searching through your dashboard manually.

Example: List the last 3 contacts.

Or: Find the contact with the email systemeio.help.demo@gmail.com.

d. Delete a contact: Instruct the AI to remove a contact from your systeme.io contact list.

Example: Remove contact with email systemeio.help.demo@gmail.com.

## 2. Managing tags

Tags help you organize your contacts, and you can manage them completely through the AI chat.

a. Create, update, or delete tags: Tell the AI to create a new tag, change an existing tag's name, or delete a tag you no longer need.

Example: Create a new tag named "My course".

b. List tags: You can ask the AI to retrieve and display a list of all your currently existing tags.

Example: List all my tags.

c. Assign tags: You can instruct the AI to manage the tags assigned to specific contacts.

Example: Assign the tag "My course" to the contact systemeio.help.demo@gmail.com.

## 3. Contact fields (custom fields)

The AI can list your available contact fields and their slugs, allowing you to use them when searching for or updating contacts.

Example: List my available contact fields and their slugs.

> Notes:
> 
> - The MCP server actions described above are available on all systeme.io plans.
> - The AI will require confirmation prompts depending on the platform you use (for example, ChatGPT may ask for permission to run the action before creating or deleting a contact).

Last updated on November 20, 2026
